content.text: {"coverage_assessment":"possible_gap","critical_or_possible_gaps":[{"gap_id":"gap_001","gap_status":"possible","missing_metadata_concept":"Temporal reference periods tied to individual measured variables or axes","proposed_field_name":"variable_temporal_coverage","evidence":"The figure title states “Restrictiveness of Services Trade Policies by GDP per capita, 2005,” while the x-axis label states “GDP per capita PPP, 2006,” and the note says GDP per capita PPP is in constant 2005 international USD.","why_snapshot_metadata":"These dates qualify the data values plotted in this scatter plot: the services trade policy restrictiveness measure and the GDP per capita measure have different explicit temporal references within the snapshot.","closest_schema_paths":["temporal_coverage.period","variables[].name","variables[].analytical_roles","variables[].unit","interpretive_notes"],"why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient":"`temporal_coverage.period` can describe the snapshot’s represented-data period but cannot associate different periods with different variables or axes. `variables[].name` could preserve labels such as “GDP per capita PPP, 2006,” but that conflates a temporal qualifier with the measured concept. `variables[].unit` can capture “constant 2005 international USD” as a unit/basis statement, and `interpretive_notes` can preserve the note text, but neither provides structured linkage between each variable and its applicable year.","material_impact":"interpretability","material_consequence":"A metadata user may not be able to tell from structured fields that the dependent policy restrictiveness measure is for 2005 while the GDP per capita predictor is for 2006, which can obscure the timing of the plotted relationship.","uncertainty_note":"The full title, axis label, and note could be preserved in existing text fields, so the materiality of requiring a separate structured variable-period mapping is uncertain."}]}

critical_or_possible_gaps.missing_metadata_concept: Temporal reference periods tied to individual measured variables or axes
critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The figure title states “Restrictiveness of Services Trade Policies by GDP per capita, 2005,” while the x-axis label states “GDP per capita PPP, 2006,” and the note says GDP per capita PPP is in constant 2005 international USD.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: These dates qualify the data values plotted in this scatter plot: the services trade policy restrictiveness measure and the GDP per capita measure have different explicit temporal references within the snapshot.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: `temporal_coverage.period` can describe the snapshot’s represented-data period but cannot associate different periods with different variables or axes. `variables[].name` could preserve labels such as “GDP per capita PPP, 2006,” but that conflates a temporal qualifier with the measured concept. `variables[].unit` can capture “constant 2005 international USD” as a unit/basis statement, and `interpretive_notes` can preserve the note text, but neither provides structured linkage between each variable and its applicable year.
critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: A metadata user may not be able to tell from structured fields that the dependent policy restrictiveness measure is for 2005 while the GDP per capita predictor is for 2006, which can obscure the timing of the plotted relationship.
critical_or_possible_gaps.uncertainty_note: The full title, axis label, and note could be preserved in existing text fields, so the materiality of requiring a separate structured variable-period mapping is uncertain.

content.text: {"coverage_assessment":"critical_gap_found","critical_or_possible_gaps":[{"gap_id":"gap_001","gap_status":"critical","missing_metadata_concept":"Variable-specific assignment to distinct y-axis scales in a dual-axis chart","proposed_field_name":"axis_scale_assignment","evidence":"The legend explicitly labels series as “Logs (left)”, “Sawnwood (right)”, “Veneer sheets (right)”, and “Plywood (right)”, while the chart displays separate left and right y-axes with different numeric ranges.","why_snapshot_metadata":"The left/right axis assignment is part of how this specific chart encodes its represented variables and is necessary to interpret the plotted series within the snapshot; it is not a general property of the parent document.","closest_schema_paths":["variables[].analytical_roles","variables[].unit","variables[].name","interpretive_notes"],"why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient":"`variables[].analytical_roles` can state that variables use a y-axis, but cannot distinguish left versus right y-axis or associate each variable with a particular scale. `variables[].unit` can record the displayed unit, but not the axis scale to use. Encoding “Logs (left)” in `variables[].name` would mix the measured concept with a presentation/scale assignment. `interpretive_notes` could preserve the legend text but would not provide structured variable-to-axis-scale metadata.","material_impact":"interpretability","material_consequence":"Users could misread the magnitude of a series by applying the wrong y-axis scale, especially because logs use the left axis and the other wood-product series use the right axis with a substantially different range.","uncertainty_note":null}]}

critical_or_possible_gaps.missing_metadata_concept: Variable-specific assignment to distinct y-axis scales in a dual-axis chart
critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The legend explicitly labels series as “Logs (left)”, “Sawnwood (right)”, “Veneer sheets (right)”, and “Plywood (right)”, while the chart displays separate left and right y-axes with different numeric ranges.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: The left/right axis assignment is part of how this specific chart encodes its represented variables and is necessary to interpret the plotted series within the snapshot; it is not a general property of the parent document.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: `variables[].analytical_roles` can state that variables use a y-axis, but cannot distinguish left versus right y-axis or associate each variable with a particular scale. `variables[].unit` can record the displayed unit, but not the axis scale to use. Encoding “Logs (left)” in `variables[].name` would mix the measured concept with a presentation/scale assignment. `interpretive_notes` could preserve the legend text but would not provide structured variable-to-axis-scale metadata.
critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: Users could misread the magnitude of a series by applying the wrong y-axis scale, especially because logs use the left axis and the other wood-product series use the right axis with a substantially different range.

Describe one critical or possibly critical v1.2 coverage gap.

Parameters
----------
gap_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
gap_status : Literal["critical", "possible"]
    Strength of the model's gap assessment.
missing_metadata_concept : str
    Reusable snapshot metadata that may not be adequately covered.
proposed_field_name : str
    Suggested snake-case label for human review, not an accepted field.
evidence : str
    Concise evidence from the supplied snapshot and document context.
why_snapshot_metadata : str
    Reason the information describes the snapshot rather than only its document.
closest_schema_paths : list[str]
    Exact v1.2 paths that most closely represent the information.
why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient : str
    Possible semantic loss when using the closest existing paths.
material_impact : Literal["interpretability", "discoverability", "both"]
    Area materially affected if the information is not covered.
material_consequence : str
    Concrete impairment caused by omission or inadequate representation.
uncertainty_note : str | None
    Remaining evidential or materiality uncertainty, if any.

critical_or_possible_gaps.missing_metadata_concept: Structured linkage between superscripted interpretive/provenance/methodological notes and the specific table components they qualify.
critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The table title and row labels carry superscripts, including “logsᵃ,” “Output real ...ᵇ,” “Foreign exchangeᶜ,” employmentᵈ, and capital costᵉ; the notes define different time bases, conversion methods, sources, and calculations for those marked components.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: The superscripted notes are embedded in the table artifact and qualify how particular represented measures in this snapshot should be interpreted; they are not general metadata about the parent document.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: `interpretive_notes` can preserve the full note text, and labels can retain superscript markers, but the schema has no structured way to state which note qualifies which title, row, variable, or measure. Snapshot-level fields such as `temporal_coverage.period`, `provenance.sources`, `analysis_methods`, and `data_collection_methods` cannot express that, for example, the 2003–2007 average applies to the input/log production volume, 2006 prices apply to foreign exchange, fieldwork collected November 2008–March 2009 applies to employment, and 2003 depreciation/exchange-rate assumptions apply to capital cost.
critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: Without scoped note linkage, metadata can either omit the target relationships or flatten them into snapshot-level descriptions, which may cause measure-specific time periods, sources, and methods to be misapplied across the whole table and may reduce discovery of snapshots by the specific temporal or provenance context attached to individual measures.
critical_or_possible_gaps.uncertainty_note: The superscript letters could be retained in free-text labels and notes, so human-readable interpretation may remain possible; the uncertainty is whether loss of structured target linkage is materially inadequate for v1.2 coverage.

critical_or_possible_gaps.missing_metadata_concept: Structured linkage between superscripted interpretive/provenance/methodological notes and the specific table components they qualify.
critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The table title and row labels carry superscripts, including “logsᵃ,” “Output real ...ᵇ,” “Foreign exchangeᶜ,” employmentᵈ, and capital costᵉ; the notes define different time bases, conversion methods, sources, and calculations for those marked components.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: The superscripted notes are embedded in the table artifact and qualify how particular represented measures in this snapshot should be interpreted; they are not general metadata about the parent document.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: `interpretive_notes` can preserve the full note text, and labels can retain superscript markers, but the schema has no structured way to state which note qualifies which title, row, variable, or measure. Snapshot-level fields such as `temporal_coverage.period`, `provenance.sources`, `analysis_methods`, and `data_collection_methods` cannot express that, for example, the 2003–2007 average applies to the input/log production volume, 2006 prices apply to foreign exchange, fieldwork collected November 2008–March 2009 applies to employment, and 2003 depreciation/exchange-rate assumptions apply to capital cost.
critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: Without scoped note linkage, metadata can either omit the target relationships or flatten them into snapshot-level descriptions, which may cause measure-specific time periods, sources, and methods to be misapplied across the whole table and may reduce discovery of snapshots by the specific temporal or provenance context attached to individual measures.
critical_or_possible_gaps.uncertainty_note: The superscript letters could be retained in free-text labels and notes, so human-readable interpretation may remain possible; the uncertainty is whether loss of structured target linkage is materially inadequate for v1.2 coverage.

content.text: {"coverage_assessment":"possible_gap","critical_or_possible_gaps":[{"gap_id":"gap_001","gap_status":"possible","missing_metadata_concept":"Explicit cartographic coordinate extent or bounding coordinates of a map snapshot","proposed_field_name":"spatial_extent_coordinates","evidence":"The map frame displays longitude and latitude graticule labels, including approximately 18°30' to 21°00' east and 40°00' to 42°30' north, around the Albania emergency road repair project map.","why_snapshot_metadata":"These coordinates describe the geographic footprint and map frame of the snapshot itself, not merely the parent document; they are visibly attached to the map artifact and define the represented spatial extent.","closest_schema_paths":["geographic_coverage.scope","geographic_coverage.locations[]","geographic_coverage.level","interpretive_notes[]"],"why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient":"`geographic_coverage.scope` and `geographic_coverage.locations[]` can record named places such as Albania and neighboring countries, but they cannot faithfully encode the explicit latitude/longitude bounding extent of the map. `interpretive_notes[]` could preserve coordinate text only as an unstructured note, losing its geospatial extent semantics.","material_impact":"both","material_consequence":"Omitting the coordinate extent can impair spatial discovery and interpretation of the map’s exact coverage, especially where the snapshot includes Albania plus bordering areas and an inset locator map rather than only a single named country.","uncertainty_note":"The materiality is plausible for map snapshots, but the named geographic coverage fields may be sufficient for some non-geospatial discovery uses."},{"gap_id":"gap_002","gap_status":"possible","missing_metadata_concept":"Cartographic distance scale or scale bar information for a map snapshot","proposed_field_name":"map_scale_bar","evidence":"The snapshot includes a scale bar labeled from 0 to 50 with the unit `KILOMETERS`.","why_snapshot_metadata":"The scale bar is part of the map snapshot and governs interpretation of distances represented in the map; Flattening the hierarchy into `variables[].name` or `dimensions[].categories` can preserve label text but not the explicit structural relationship between totals, subcomponents, and repeated child labels under different parents.","material_impact":"interpretability","material_consequence":"Without the nested structure, users may be unable to distinguish component categories from peer indicators or determine which parent measure repeated labels such as “IBRD” and “IDA” belong to, which can materially impair interpretation of the represented table measures.","uncertainty_note":"The impact is assessed as possible because some hierarchy could be partially preserved by concatenating full label paths in variable names, though that would not provide structured reusable hierarchy metadata."}]}

critical_or_possible_gaps.missing_metadata_concept: Explicit multi-level row or category hierarchy within the snapshot's statistical tables
critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The snapshot shows nested table structures such as “TRADE” → “Total exports (fob)” → “Coffee / Tea / Manufactures” and “EXTERNAL DEBT and RESOURCE FLOWS” → “Total debt outstanding and disbursed” → “IBRD / IDA”, with repeated labels like “IBRD” and “IDA” under different parent measures.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: The hierarchy is visibly part of the snapshot's own table organization and is needed to understand how represented indicators and categories relate within this composite figure; it is not merely metadata about the parent document.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: `dimensions[].category_groups[]` supports only one nonrecursive grouping level, while this snapshot uses nested parent-child row structures. Flattening the hierarchy into `variables[].name` or `dimensions[].categories` can preserve label text but not the explicit structural relationship between totals, subcomponents, and repeated child labels under different parents.
critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: Without the nested structure, users may be unable to distinguish component categories from peer indicators or determine which parent measure repeated labels such as “IBRD” and “IDA” belong to, which can materially impair interpretation of the represented table measures.
critical_or_possible_gaps.uncertainty_note: The impact is assessed as possible because some hierarchy could be partially preserved by concatenating full label paths in variable names, though that would not provide structured reusable hierarchy metadata.

These panels use different variables, time periods, and comparison structures.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: The panel/section organization is part of the visible analytical object itself and determines how the snapshot's represented data are interpreted; it is not merely metadata about the parent project document.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: The schema can list panel titles and separately list variables, dimensions, temporal coverage, visualization types, comparisons, and notes, but it cannot bind those metadata elements to the particular panel or section where they apply. A flat representation may lose which variables, periods, and comparators belong to the development diamond versus the economic-ratio diamond, line charts, or tabular sections.

critical_or_possible_gaps.missing_metadata_concept: Cartographic scale or distance scale for a map snapshot
critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The snapshot includes dual scale bars labeled “MILES” with 0, 25, 50 and “KILOMETERS” with 0, 25, 50, 75.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: The scale bars are part of the map artifact itself and describe how distances in the represented geography should be interpreted within this snapshot, not merely the parent document.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: `visualization_types[]` can identify the object as a map, and `geographic_coverage` can identify Jordan or displayed locations, but neither records the map’s distance scale. `variables[].unit` can represent units but only as qualifiers of measured variables, not cartographic distance scale. `interpretive_notes[]` could preserve a textual description of the scale bar, but it would not distinguish scale as reusable structured map metadata.
critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: Without an adequate way to record the map scale, users may be unable to interpret distances, proximity, or spatial extent represented by the map from the metadata alone.
critical_or_possible_gaps.uncertainty_note: The scale could be retained as an interpretive note, so the gap depends on whether structured cartographic scale is considered materially necessary rather than merely useful for map snapshots.

critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The financing section visibly nests row categories: “World Bank Group Financing” contains “International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)”; “Non-World Bank Group Financing” contains “Trust Funds,” which in turn contains “Reform and Reconstruction in Iraq MDTF.”

critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: Users may misinterpret the 2002 tariff, consumption, charges, income, and affordability percentages as observed data rather than projected or scenario-based values, affecting interpretation of the table’s meaning.
critical_or_possible_gaps.uncertainty_note: The word “Future” is explicit, but the snapshot does not state the projection method or explicitly use the term “projected”; existing dimension/category source text may be considered adequate for preserving the distinction.

critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: Without preserving the explicit linkage structure, metadata users may know the figure concerns expenditure totals but not the intended relationship among the displayed concepts, making the chart’s analytical structure harder to interpret without viewing the image.
critical_or_possible_gaps.uncertainty_note: The impact may be mitigated by `visualization_types`, `subject_summary`, and listed variables/categories, so it is uncertain whether a separate structured relationship field is materially necessary.

critical_or_possible_gaps.missing_metadata_concept: Panel-specific semantic metadata associations for a composite snapshot, especially which temporal coverage, measured concept, and visualization form apply to each panel.
critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The snapshot contains multiple titled analytical panels with different scopes: “Known Hazardous Areas and Number of Known Hazards as of 31 March 2016,” “Types of Hazards - as of 31 March 2016,” “MRE* Audiences: January - March 2016,” and “Hazardous Areas Dec2013 - Mar2016.”
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: These panel headings and their associated variables and time periods are part of the snapshot artifact itself and determine how the data displayed in each subfigure should be interpreted; they are not merely parent-document metadata.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: The schema can list panel titles, variables, visualization types, dimensions, and one snapshot-level temporal coverage, and it can preserve explanatory text in interpretive_notes. However, it cannot explicitly bind each panel to its own temporal coverage, measured concepts, dimensions, and visualization type. A flat representation could list all periods and variables but lose which period applies to which panel, or compress the periods into a single temporal_coverage expression that obscures distinct as-of and interval meanings.
critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: Without panel-level associations, a metadata record could imply that all displayed variables share the same time period or visualization context, making the map, hazard-type donut chart, MRE audience donut chart, and hazardous-area trend chart difficult to interpret correctly as separate analytical components of one composite figure.

Collapsing all locations into `geographic_coverage.locations[]` could imply that every listed location applies to every displayed population category; encoding the full phrase in `variables[].name` mixes the measured concept with its geographic qualifier and reduces semantic clarity.","material_impact":"both","material_consequence":"A metadata record could lose or misrepresent the scope of individual headline statistics, making it unclear that the IDP figure is limited to Burkina Faso, Mali, and western Niger while the refugees/asylum-seekers figure covers a different country set. critical_or_possible_gaps.missing_metadata_concept: Structured association between each displayed measured concept or population category and its explicitly stated geographic qualifier within a multi-statistic snapshot.
critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The snapshot separately labels headline figures as “REFUGEES AND ASYLUM-SEEKERS IN BURKINA FASO, CHAD, MALI, MAURITANIA AND NIGER” and “IDPs IN BURKINA FASO, MALI AND WESTERN NIGER,” while other displayed categories are “IDP AND REFUGEE RETURNEES” and “OTHER PEOPLE OF CONCERN.”
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: The geographic phrases are visibly attached to specific displayed measures in the snapshot and define the scope of those represented data, rather than merely describing the parent UNHCR report.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: Existing fields can list measured concepts and locations at the snapshot level, or fold geography into a variable name as text, but they do not structure which locations qualify which specific measured concept. Collapsing all locations into `geographic_coverage.locations[]` could imply that every listed location applies to every displayed population category; encoding the full phrase in `variables[].name` mixes the measured concept with its geographic qualifier and reduces semantic clarity.
critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: A metadata record could lose or misrepresent the scope of individual headline statistics, making it unclear that the IDP figure is limited to Burkina Faso, Mali, and western Niger while the refugees/asylum-seekers figure covers a different country set. This can impair interpretation of the snapshot and discovery of snapshots about a specific population-location combination.
critical_or_possible_gaps.uncertainty_note: This may overlap with modeling individual observations or data labels, which are partly outside the schema scope; the gap is possible because the qualifier association is non-numeric and interpretively important, but its materiality as reusable metadata requires human review.

critical_or_possible_gaps.missing_metadata_concept: Non-textual pictogram labels used as table column headers or category identifiers
critical_or_possible_gaps.evidence: The table has three numeric columns headed only by pictograms: an older person with a cane, a walking person with a cane, and a wheelchair user icon; no textual column labels or legend are visible in the snapshot.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_snapshot_metadata: The pictograms are part of the table itself and appear to define the categories for the displayed numeric columns, so they describe how the snapshot’s represented data are organized rather than only describing the parent document.
critical_or_possible_gaps.why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient: `dimensions[].categories` and `dimensions[].category_groups[].categories` represent source-grounded terms but are oriented toward textual or normalized category terms; using them for icon-only headers would require inventing a text description or normalized category meaning not explicitly stated. `interpretive_notes` can preserve explicit notes, but there is no explicit note or legend. `visualization_types` can identify the artifact as a table but not preserve the semantic role of icon-only column headers.
critical_or_possible_gaps.material_consequence: If the icon-only column headers cannot be represented faithfully, users may know the row indicators and counts but not what the three numeric columns distinguish, materially impairing interpretation of the table’s measures.
critical_or_possible_gaps.uncertainty_note: The pictograms’ exact intended categories are not textually defined in the visible snapshot; human review is needed to decide whether descriptive encoding in existing category fields is sufficient or would over-interpret the source.

schema_.description:
Represent one confirmatory Schema v1.2 coverage assessment.

Parameters
----------
coverage_assessment : Literal["no_critical_gap_found", "critical_gap_found", "possible_gap"]
    Snapshot-level coverage result.
critical_or_possible_gaps : list[CandidateGap]
    Evidence-backed gaps for later human adjudication.
schema_.title: SchemaValidationResult

CandidateGap.description:
Describe one critical or possibly critical v1.2 coverage gap.

Parameters
----------
gap_id : str
    Identifier unique within the snapshot assessment.
gap_status : Literal["critical", "possible"]
    Strength of the model's gap assessment.
missing_metadata_concept : str
    Reusable snapshot metadata that may not be adequately covered.
proposed_field_name : str
    Suggested snake-case label for human review, not an accepted field.
evidence : str
    Concise evidence from the supplied snapshot and document context.
why_snapshot_metadata : str
    Reason the information describes the snapshot rather than only its document.
closest_schema_paths : list[str]
    Exact v1.2 paths that most closely represent the information.
why_existing_fields_may_be_insufficient : str
    Possible semantic loss when using the closest existing paths.
material_impact : Literal["interpretability", "discoverability", "both"]
    Area materially affected if the information is not covered.
material_consequence : str
    Concrete impairment caused by omission or inadequate representation.
uncertainty_note : str | None
    Remaining evidential or materiality uncertainty, if any.
